questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the IUCN Red List update of 9 April 2026:
1. The emperor penguin was moved from Near Threatened to Endangered.
2. The Antarctic fur seal was moved from Least Concern to Endangered.
3. The southern elephant seal was moved from Least Concern to Critically Endangered.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The southern elephant seal was moved to Vulnerable, not Critically Endangered. The assessment links the declines to record-low Antarctic sea ice, and avian influenza killed over 90 per cent of newborn elephant seal pups in some colonies. The IUCN is headquartered in Gland, Switzerland.
questions.s: IUCN and Good Morning America, 9 Apr 2026

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Shekha Jheel Bird Sanctuary:
1. It was designated a Wetland of International Importance under the Ramsar Convention on 22 April 2026, taking India's Ramsar sites to 99.
2. The freshwater wetland in the Gangetic plains is a stopover on the Central Asian Flyway and hosts bar-headed goose and painted stork.
3. The Ramsar Convention was adopted in 1975 at Geneva.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The sanctuary lies in Aligarh, Uttar Pradesh, and took shape after the Upper Ganga Canal was built in 1852. The Ramsar Convention on Wetlands was adopted in 1971 at Ramsar, Iran, and entered into force in 1975, so the Geneva claim is wrong.
questions.s: Drishti IAS, IAS Baba and Swarajya, 22 Apr 2026

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the third synchronised Nilgiri tahr survey of April 2026:
1. The Tamil Nadu Forest Department, together with Kerala, counted 1,364 Nilgiri tahr in Tamil Nadu.
2. The Nilgiri tahr is the state animal of Tamil Nadu.
3. The species is endemic to the Eastern Ghats.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Nilgiri tahr (Nilgiritragus hylocrius) is endemic to the Western Ghats, and Eravikulam National Park in Kerala holds the largest population. The survey, run from 24 to 27 April under Project Nilgiri Tahr, found most of the Tamil Nadu animals in the Anamalai Hills and the Nilgiris.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026:
1. They came into effect on 1 April 2026 and require four-stream segregation of waste at source into wet, dry, sanitary and special-care waste.
2. They have been framed under the Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974.
3. They introduce an Extended Bulk Waste Generator Responsibility framework.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Rules are framed under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986, which is the umbrella law for most waste rules. They also add a centralised online monitoring portal and buffer zones for facilities above five tonnes per day.

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs of places in the news in April 2026 (Place : Feature):
1. Wular Lake : Largest freshwater lake in India, on the Jhelum River in Jammu and Kashmir
2. Raimona National Park : Kokrajhar district of Assam, on the India-Bhutan border
3. Namdapha National Park : Changlang district of Arunachal Pradesh, on the India-Myanmar border
4. Kali Tiger Reserve : Comprising Dandeli Wildlife Sanctuary and Anshi National Park in Kerala
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: Pair 4 is wrong: the Kali Tiger Reserve, around which an Eco-Sensitive Zone was proposed in April 2026, comprises Dandeli Wildlife Sanctuary and Anshi National Park in Uttara Kannada district of Karnataka, and the Kali River flows through it. Raimona is contiguous with Bhutan's Phibsoo Wildlife Sanctuary, and Wular was designated a Ramsar site in 1990.

questions.q: Olive Ridley turtles tagged in Tamil Nadu were tracked migrating towards the Sri Lanka Dome in April 2026. Which one of the following statements about the Olive Ridley turtle is correct?
o: It is the smallest and most abundant sea turtle, known for mass nesting called arribada, and is listed as Vulnerable on the IUCN Red List
It is the largest living sea turtle and is listed as Critically Endangered on the IUCN Red List
It nests only singly, never in mass nesting, and its largest rookery is on the Gujarat coast
It is protected only under Schedule IV of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972
questions.e: The Olive Ridley is the smallest and most abundant sea turtle, and Odisha's Gahirmatha is the world's largest sea turtle rookery. It is in Schedule I of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972, the highest protection. The leatherback, not the Olive Ridley, is the largest sea turtle.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Hindu Kush Himalaya (HKH) region:
1. An ICIMOD report in April 2026 said the region recorded a record drop in snow persistence.
2. The region spans eight countries, is called the Third Pole, and is the source of ten major Asian river systems.
3. ICIMOD is headquartered in Thimphu, Bhutan.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: ICIMOD, the International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development, is based in Kathmandu, Nepal. The HKH is called the Third Pole because its snow and ice feed the headwaters of those major river systems.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. In April 2026 the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change released draft rules to manage tar balls and protect coastlines from oil spills.
2. The Arogya Van initiative to plant medicinal trees along National Highways is run by the Ministry of Ayush.
3. Tar balls are weathered blobs of oil carried by currents and waves to the shore.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Arogya Van initiative was announced by the National Highways Authority of India under the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways, with priority sites near toll plazas, wayside amenities and interchanges. Tar balls form when crude oil from spills or ship operations weathers at sea.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Indian monsoon forecast for 2026:
1. On 29 May 2026 the India Meteorological Department cut its forecast for the southwest monsoon season to 90 per cent of the Long Period Average.
2. At 90 per cent of the Long Period Average, the season was placed in the 'deficient' category.
3. The IMD had issued its first long-range forecast for the season on 13 April 2026.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: IMD places a season at 90 to 95 per cent of the LPA in the 'below normal' category and below 90 per cent as 'deficient', so 90 per cent sits at the edge of below normal, with a 60 per cent probability of deficient rainfall. The forecast also warned of a hotter-than-normal June.
questions.s: Down To Earth and IMD, 29 May 2026

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the cheetah introduction programme:
1. Two female cheetahs from Botswana were released from quarantine into the wild at Kuno National Park on 11 May 2026.
2. Project Cheetah began in September 2022 with cheetahs brought from South Africa.
3. Kuno National Park is located in Sheopur district of Madhya Pradesh.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Project Cheetah began in September 2022 with cheetahs from Namibia, and South African cheetahs followed in 2023. India's cheetah population stood at 57 after the release, including cubs born in India.
questions.s: All India Radio and The Hitavada, 11 May 2026

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Hollongapar Gibbon Sanctuary:
1. A Western hoolock gibbon was documented crossing an artificial canopy bridge over a railway line for the first time, as reported in May 2026.
2. The bridges were designed by the Wildlife Institute of India with the Assam Forest Department and Northeast Frontier Railway.
3. The sanctuary is located in Tinsukia district of Assam.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The sanctuary is in Jorhat district, and the Lumding-Dibrugarh railway line cuts through it. The canopy bridges were installed in February-March 2025, and the hoolock gibbon is India's only ape.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Central Ridge of Delhi:
1. In May 2026 the Delhi government issued a final notification under Section 20 of the Indian Forest Act, 1927 declaring about 670 hectares of the Central Ridge a Reserved Forest.
2. Reserved Forest status gives the highest statutory protection under the Act, prohibiting grazing, hunting and timber extraction unless authorised.
3. The Delhi Ridge is an extension of the Satpura range.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Ridge is the northern extension of the ancient Aravalli range. Under the Indian Forest Act, 1927, a final notification under Section 20 completes the process that begins with a notification of intention under Section 4.
questions.s: Chronicle India and Drishti IAS, May 2026

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the International Day for Biological Diversity, 22 May 2026:
1. The theme was 'Acting locally for global impact'.
2. The Day marks the entry into force of the Convention on Biological Diversity in 1993.
3. The Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework, adopted at COP15, has 23 targets for 2030.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Day marks the adoption of the text of the Convention on Biological Diversity in 1992, not its entry into force. The Framework was adopted at COP15 in Montreal in December 2022 and has four goals for 2050; countries submit National Biodiversity Strategies and Action Plans to implement it ahead of COP17.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about wildlife records from Arunachal Pradesh in May 2026:
1. A Royal Bengal tiger was recorded by camera traps in D'Ering Memorial Wildlife Sanctuary, the first confirmed evidence there since 2005.
2. The dragonfly Gynacantha khasiaca was rediscovered in Namdapha National Park and Tiger Reserve after about 110 years.
3. Namdapha lies in Lohit district.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Namdapha lies in Changlang district. D'Ering Memorial Wildlife Sanctuary is near Pasighat in East Siang district, between the Siang and Sibya rivers. The dragonfly, last recorded in the Abor Hills in 1914, is assessed as Data Deficient by the IUCN.
questions.s: EastMojo, UNI and ETV Bharat, 8-27 May 2026

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Union government's affidavit in the Supreme Court on 19 May 2026 on hydropower in the upper Ganga basin:
1. It said that no new hydropower projects should be permitted in the Alaknanda-Bhagirathi basin, allowing only seven already approved projects to proceed.
2. It proposed a minimum flow of 1,000 cusecs on the Alaknanda, Bhagirathi and Mandakini.
3. The Alaknanda and Bhagirathi meet at Rudraprayag to form the Ganga.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Alaknanda and Bhagirathi meet at Devprayag to form the Ganga; Rudraprayag is where the Mandakini joins the Alaknanda. The affidavit was filed jointly by the Environment, Power and Jal Shakti Ministries, and of the seven projects four are operational and three under construction.
questions.s: Down To Earth and Outlook India, 19 May 2026

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about wetland protection in Maharashtra:
1. By May 2026 the National Centre for Sustainable Coastal Management had completed ground-truthing of more than 23,000 wetlands in the State.
2. Notification of the verified wetlands would be done under the Wetlands (Conservation and Management) Rules framework.
3. The National Centre for Sustainable Coastal Management is an institution under the Ministry of Jal Shakti.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The NCSCM is an institution under the Ministry of Earth Sciences, not Jal Shakti. Ground-truthing, the physical verification of satellite-mapped wetlands, is the step that precedes formal notification and legal protection.
questions.s: Deccan Herald and NEXT IAS, 19 May 2026

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Mount Everest in the spring 2026 season:
1. A record 274 climbers reached the summit from the Nepal side in a single day on 20 May 2026, surpassing the earlier record of 223 in 2019.
2. Mount Everest lies on the India-China border.
3. Nepal issued a record 495 Everest permits in the season.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Everest (8,848.86 m) lies on the Nepal-China border, and its main summit routes are the southeast ridge from Nepal and the northeast ridge from Tibet. About 150 of the 274 summiteers on 20 May were Nepali Sherpas.
questions.s: Alan Arnette and ETV Bharat, 20 May 2026

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Ramsar sites in India:
1. Jai Prakash Narayan Bird Sanctuary (Surha Tal) in Ballia district, Uttar Pradesh was announced as India's 100th Ramsar site around World Environment Day 2026.
2. India ranks third in the world by number of Ramsar sites, behind the United Kingdom and Mexico.
3. Uttar Pradesh now has 12 Ramsar sites.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Surha Tal is Uttar Pradesh's 13th Ramsar site; the State had 12 after Shekha Jheel was designated on 22 April 2026. The sanctuary, declared in 1991, hosts sarus cranes, bar-headed geese and the fishing cat.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about E85 fuel launched on World Environment Day, 5 June 2026:
1. It was launched by Petroleum Minister Hardeep Singh Puri at an IndianOil outlet in Delhi for flex-fuel vehicles.
2. E85 is a blend of 85 per cent petrol and 15 per cent ethanol.
3. Petrol blending with ethanol in India has reached 20 per cent (E20).
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: E85 is the reverse: it is largely ethanol (about 85 per cent) blended with petrol, and it needs flex-fuel engines, unlike E20 which ordinary petrol vehicles can use. The roll-out is to expand to about 500 outlets by December 2026.
questions.s: Business Today and Outlook Business, 5 Jun 2026

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about El Nino:
1. On 11 June 2026 the US NOAA announced that El Nino conditions had formed in the equatorial Pacific, upgrading its outlook from an El Nino Watch to an El Nino Advisory.
2. El Nino is the warm phase of the El Nino-Southern Oscillation and is usually associated with weaker Indian monsoon rainfall.
3. El Nino is marked by cooling of sea surface temperatures in the central and eastern equatorial Pacific.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: El Nino is the warming of the central and eastern equatorial Pacific, which weakens the Walker circulation and the trade winds; the cooling phase is La Nina. This is why NOAA's declaration added to concern after the IMD's below-normal monsoon forecast of 90 per cent of the LPA.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about India's first national assessment of floating solar potential, released in June 2026:
1. It was prepared by the National Institute of Solar Energy and estimates over 102 GWp across water bodies.
2. The National Institute of Solar Energy is an autonomous institution under the Ministry of Power.
3. Maharashtra tops the five States with the highest floating solar potential.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: NISE is an autonomous institution under the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy. Maharashtra is followed by Madhya Pradesh, Karnataka, Odisha and Telangana, and the assessment takes India's total assessed solar potential to 3,445 GWp.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the 64th sessions of the UN climate subsidiary bodies (SB64) at Bonn in June 2026:
1. They ended on 18 June without agreement on the global goal on adaptation, which was passed to COP31 under rule 16.
2. The dispute concerned whether to refer to the COP30 pledge to at least triple adaptation finance by 2035.
3. The sessions concluded with a final agreement on indicators for the global goal on adaptation.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The target to triple adaptation finance survived only in brackets, so the goal was handed to COP31. The subsidiary bodies are the SBSTA and SBI, which prepare decisions for the Conference of the Parties; Parties did agree texts on a just transition mechanism.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the UN climate conference calendar:
1. COP31 is to be held in Antalya, Turkey, from 9 to 20 November 2026, with Australia serving as president of negotiations.
2. COP30 was held in Brasilia, Brazil.
3. COP32 is to be held in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, in 2027.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: COP30 was held in Belem, Brazil, the gateway to the Amazon. Parties at Bonn also agreed a package on the Belem-Antalya mechanism for just transition support, named after the COP30 and COP31 host cities.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Noida International Airport at Jewar:
1. It began commercial flight operations on 15 June 2026, with IndiGo operating the first scheduled service from Lucknow.
2. It is operated by Yamuna International Airport Private Limited, an SPV of Zurich Airport.
3. It is located in Ghaziabad district of Uttar Pradesh.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The airport is in Gautam Buddh Nagar district. Phase I is designed for about 12 million passengers a year, with a single runway, and Zurich Airport holds a 40-year concession to develop and operate it.
questions.s: ETV Bharat and Air Power Asia, 15 Jun 2026

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Kailash Mansarovar Yatra 2026:
1. 1,000 yatris selected by a computerised draw travel in 20 batches of 50.
2. The Yatra uses the Lipulekh and Nathu La passes.
3. The Lipulekh pass lies in Sikkim.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Lipulekh lies in Uttarakhand (in Pithoragarh district on the border with Tibet) and Nathu La in Sikkim. The Ministry of External Affairs organises the Yatra, which runs from June to August and has both routes fully motorable with very little trekking.
